_why: What each demo block's controls really are, read off a real FM3 (firmware 13.0) through the relay on
2026-09-23 — GET /preset/blocks/{eid}/params, nothing written — so the demo's Delay shows a delay's
controls and not the amp's tone stack. "Input, Compressor, Wah, Cab, Delay, Reverb, and Output all
displayed the same generic controls: Mix, Drive 1, Tone, Bass, Mid, Treble."
The amp keeps its own file, amp-params.json, captured the same way earlier.
comp is the one exception: no preset on the unit that night was live with a Compressor in it, and
loading one to read it would have changed what was on his rig. Its ranges and starting values are
the FM3's own tables (forgefx-midi src/gen3/fm3/ranges.generated.ts — the table the unit's live read
converts through), and its pages are FM3-Edit's for the Studio FF type.
`pages` is each block's editor pages as the unit sent them (the params read's `layout`), cut down to
the page names and the parameter ids in each page's parameter rows. The demo hands them back as a
layout so EDIT splits a demo block into the same pages as a real one (lib/editPages.js).
